item.name: Submit a transaction and score it for fraud

request.name: Submit a transaction and score it for fraud

description.content:
Runs the transaction through the hybrid fraud engine
(`analyzeTransactionHybrid`): hard rules first (can force
`risk_level: "high"` regardless of the model), then the ML
service (with SHAP explanation), falling back to the deterministic
rule engine only if the ML service is unreachable. If the result
is medium or high risk, an alert is created automatically
(pushed over WebSocket as `alert:new`) and any of the caller's
active webhooks subscribed to `transaction.flagged` are fired
(fire-and-forget — see "Webhooks" below).

Accepts either a JWT bearer token or an API key (`X-API-Key` —
see "API Keys" below); a key needs the `transactions:write`
scope. Also accepts an optional `Idempotency-Key` header so a
network retry can't double-submit — see "Idempotency" below.

Opt-in. Same key + same request body within the TTL
(`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL_HOURS`, default 24h) replays the
original response instead of reprocessing (the response
carries an `Idempotent-Replay: true` header on replay);
same key + a different body returns 409.

info.name: FraudGuard API
info.description:
REST API for FraudGuard — a hybrid rules + ML transaction fraud-detection system.

Quick start:
1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable if not running on the default (http://localhost:5000/api/v1).
2. Run auth > login (pre-filled with the seeded admin/admin123 credentials, or register your own user first) — its test script auto-saves the returned accessToken/refreshToken into the bearerToken/refreshToken collection variables, which every other request already references via collection-level Bearer auth. No manual token copy-pasting needed. If the account has 2FA enabled, login instead returns a mfaToken (auto-saved) — run "Complete login with a TOTP or backup code" next with the code from your authenticator app.
3. Try transactions > "Submit a transaction and score it for fraud" — the example body is tuned to trip the crypto/prepaid/unknown-location risk factors so you see a non-trivial fraud_score and shap_explanation right away.
4. Try alerts > "Resolve an alert with an analyst verdict" — verdict is required (confirmed_fraud or false_positive), which is what actually drives the dynamic device/IP blacklist described in docs/METHODOLOGY.md. Try alerts > "Resolve up to 100 alerts in one request" to bulk-resolve, or alerts > export / transactions > export / admin > audit-logs > export for CSV downloads.
5. Try auth > mfa > setup, then mfa > enable with the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, to turn on 2FA for the logged-in account (scan the QR code in the response body, or copy the "secret" field into an app manually).
6. Forgot/reset password and email verification links are logged to the backend console (no SMTP configured by default) — copy the token out of the log line and paste it into reset-password / verify-email.
7. Try api-keys > "Create an API key for your own account" (optionally with expiresInDays) — its test script auto-saves the returned key into the apiKey collection variable. Set an X-API-Key header to {{apiKey}} on transactions requests to call them as a service integration instead of a logged-in session.
8. Try webhooks > "Register a webhook for your own account" (e.g. with a webhook.site URL) to see signed "transaction.flagged" deliveries fire the next time you submit a medium/high-risk transaction — check webhooks > {id} > deliveries afterward. A failed delivery retries automatically (survives a server restart).
9. Try auth > me > export > "Download a JSON bundle..." for a self-service data export, or auth > me > "Delete (anonymize) your own account" to see account deletion (requires your password).
10. admin > * and alerts > "Assign or unassign an alert" require the logged-in user to have the admin role (the seeded admin account does) — admin also sees every user's api-keys/webhooks by default (pass ?mine=true to scope to just your own).
11. GET {{baseUrl}}/../../metrics (i.e. http://localhost:5000/metrics, outside /api entirely) returns Prometheus-format metrics — not part of this collection since it is unauthenticated and outside the API surface.

Generated from docs/openapi.yaml — see that file (or README.md "Architecture") for full schemas, and docs/METHODOLOGY.md for how the fraud engine actually decides risk_level.
